# Part 0 — CSR Core


> **About this draft.** This is the shared core section that appears in full in the unified manual and in every standalone department extract. It follows the Stage 0 conventions: section numbers as `§0-n`, cross-references as `§x-y`, callouts typed as Policy / Watch-out / Script / Note / Critical.
>
> Two markers appear throughout:
> **Escalation targets render as the current role holder, linked to the escalation directory.
> **`[VERIFY: Vn]`** — content depending on an open verification question.
>
> On approval this splits into `src/p0/01-*.md` through `src/p0/12-*.md`.

---

## §0-1 How to use this part

Part 0 is the core of the manual: procedures that apply to **every call**, whatever the department.
It appears in full in every copy, including single-department extracts, alongside Part 1.

How the manual is organised, how section numbers work, and what each kind of callout means are
set out on the front page — see **How to use this manual**.

> **Policy — department parts can override this one.** Where a department part contradicts Part 0,
> the department part wins — but only where it says explicitly that it is overriding. One example is
> in [[§0-6]]: out-of-pocket purchases normally need no paperwork, but respiratory equipment
> overrides that.

---

## §0-2 Status update for a DME order

Most inbound calls are status requests. Work this decision tree in order.

### §0-2.1 Before anything else

Match the caller's patient to a file using **name and date of birth**.

If you can't find the patient, **search the caller's phone number**. A match on a **lead** means a Sales team member is already working with this caller — usually for a power mobility device or PAP — even though no account exists yet. Get the caller to the Sales team member named in the lead notes, or the relevant Sales queue if they're unavailable — the Sales Q for power mobility, the PAP Q for PAP. See [[§9-4]].

If the phone number finds nothing either, treat it as the first branch below rather than assuming an order exists.

### §0-2.2 Decision tree

{{diagram:status-tree}}

| What you find | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **No patient in the system** | The referral was likely never received, or arrived too recently for an order to exist | Tell the caller we'll update them once the order is created. If the caller is the provider's office, ask them to resend the referral. |
| **Order received recently, no updates** | Still in early review | Tell the caller the information is under review, and that we'll request any additional documentation once insurance verification is complete. |
| **Additional documentation requested** | We're waiting on the provider | Open the `Transaction` tab and click **Fax History**. Compare the most recent documentation request against the most recent documents received. Tell the caller specifically what's outstanding. |
| **Pending authorization** | Submitted; waiting on the insurance decision | Tell the caller we're awaiting insurance approval before delivery. Authorization questions go to the relevant intake team's authorization members — for Manual Mobility, `[ROLE: Authorization Escalation — Manual Mobility]`. See [[§0-12.2]]. |
| **Order needs to be re-opened** | Requires review before anyone can commit | Do **not** transfer. Email the department queue. The team reviews first and would tell the caller the same thing. |

> **Watch-out** — When checking documentation status, confirm *how* the request was sent. Requests go out by fax, **email**, or through **Parachute/SutureSign** — on any order type — and a provider who says they never received anything may be looking in the wrong place.

> **Note** — Power Mobility orders move through a different sequence and their status language differs. See [[§4-1]] for the Power process overview.

### §0-2.3 What not to say

- Don't estimate a delivery date that isn't in the system
- Don't promise a callback within a specific window unless you're the one making the call
- Don't attribute a delay to the provider's office by name to the patient

## §0-3 Updating patient information

### §0-3.1 Demographics and contact details

Height, weight, date of birth, phone, email, address:

1. Update directly on the `Patient` tab
2. Leave a note recording what changed and who reported it

No transfer or email is needed. This is yours to complete on the call.

### §0-3.2 Insurance changes

1. Notate the **plan name**, **member ID**, and **effective date**
2. Add the details on the `Insurance` tab of the Transaction Workflow
3. Optionally confirm on the `Eligibility` tab — helpful, not required

> **Watch-out** — Collect all three fields before ending the call. A plan name without a member ID and effective date usually means someone has to call the patient back.

---

## §0-4 Insurance plan names

Many plan names look nearly identical but belong to different groups.

Check the **number shown next to the plan**. Matching numbers mean the same group; different numbers mean different groups, regardless of how similar the names look.

If you can't tell which plan applies, leave the insurance information you collected in the notes for the intake team rather than guessing. A wrong plan selection is harder to unwind than an unanswered question.

---

## §0-5 Finding information on equipment

Use the **Item Master** to look up equipment.

> **Watch-out** — Item Master search is sensitive to phrasing. If your first search returns nothing useful, try several variations before concluding we don't carry the item.

When a caller wants detail on a specific product:

1. Search the model together with the manufacturer name
2. Offer to send a link to the manufacturer's product page by text or email

Some items share a HCPCS code with a different product, so a code search can return more than one thing. Where that's true it's noted in the relevant department part.

Equipment specifications also appear in the department parts: manual mobility and general DME from [[§2-3]] onward, power mobility at [[§4-10]], respiratory equipment from [[§3-5]] onward, and oxygen at [[§7-5]].

---

## §0-6 Out-of-pocket purchases

When a patient buys equipment outright, we aren't submitting to insurance, so **no referral paperwork is required**.

> **Policy — the CSR team handles out-of-pocket purchases.** Rather than transferring the caller, complete the purchase and then send **one email to all three departments** so each can act on it:
>
> | Notify | Why |
> |---|---|
> | The **intake** team for the equipment — for a power chair, the **Power intake** team | To open the order |
> | The **eligibility** team | So no insurance verification is started |
> | **Field Operations** | To schedule delivery |

Use the standard subject format from [[§0-11.2]] — for example, `OOP Purchase: Maria Garcia 456789`.

Out-of-pocket pricing is in the Item Master.

> **Policy — no sales tax unless stated.** Quote out-of-pocket prices **without** sales tax unless otherwise stated; most of what we sell is exempt.

> **Policy — no insurance is not a barrier, but assistance doesn't apply.** A patient without insurance can still purchase equipment. However, an out-of-pocket order is **ineligible for the Economic Assistance Application and for a payment plan** — see [[§10-20.6]].

> **Policy — respiratory exception.** Oxygen concentrators, PAP devices (CPAP and BiPAP), and ventilators require a prescription **even when purchased out of pocket** — federal law restricts their sale to a prescriber's order. This overrides the general rule above. See [[§3-2]].

---

## §0-7 Insurance acceptance

For general "do you take my insurance" questions, advise the caller to have a referral sent for review. Most insurances are accepted, but acceptance depends on the specific plan and item rather than the carrier alone.

> **Policy — what a secondary covers.** If the **primary** denies an item, a secondary generally cannot pick up the full cost — secondary coverage usually applies to the remaining cost-sharing on items the primary approved.
>
> **Medicaid is the exception.** Texas Medicaid covers some items Medicare never does — shower chairs, tub transfer benches, incontinence supplies — and can pay for them as secondary for a dual-eligible patient. See [[§2-8]] and [[§3-8]].

> **Script** — "We accept most major insurances, but coverage depends on your specific plan and the item being requested, so the most reliable way to find out is to have your doctor's office send the referral over. Once we verify your benefits we'll be able to tell you exactly what's covered."


### §0-7.1 Coverage exceptions at a glance

A few items are covered only in Texas, a few aren't covered anywhere, and one is often wrongly assumed to be Texas-only.

**Covered only in Texas**

| Item | Basis | Otherwise | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lift chair | TX Medicaid Waiver Program | Not available | [[§2-8.1]] |
| Shower chair | TX Medicaid | Out-of-pocket | [[§2-8.3]] |
| Tub transfer bench | TX Medicaid | Out-of-pocket | [[§2-8.3]] |
| Incontinence supplies | TX Medicaid (TMHP) | Not covered | [[§3-8.1]] |

{{flag:tx-medicaid-only|capacity_lbs,seat,dimensions,product_weight_lbs,notes,+part,+Sizing}}

> **Watch-out — "Texas Medicaid" and "the Texas Medicaid Waiver Program" are not the same thing.** Shower chairs and incontinence supplies fall under the former; lift chairs under the latter. A patient with TX Medicaid does not automatically qualify for a lift chair.

**Not covered anywhere**

| Item | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Raised toilet seat | Out-of-pocket only | [[§2-8.3]] |
| Knee walker | Out-of-pocket, except through VGM Homelink | [[§2-6]] |
| Ramps | Out-of-pocket only | [[§4-11]] |
| Portable oxygen concentrators | Not carried | [[§7-5]] |
| Diabetic supplies | Not carried | |
| Breast pumps | Not carried | |
| Truck or vehicle lifts for a PMD | Not offered | [[§4-11]] |

**Often assumed to be Texas-only, but isn't**

| Item | Coverage | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 3-in-1 commode chair | Can be covered by Medicare | [[§2-8.3]] |

> **Watch-out — not every bathroom item is Texas-only.** The 3-in-1 commode can be covered by Medicare anywhere. See [[§2-8.3]].

> **Note — coverage is not the only constraint.** An item can be covered by a patient's plan and still be undeliverable, because every order must fall inside the delivery radius for that item. See [[§2-2.1]].

## §0-8 Standard order process

Most orders follow this sequence:

| Step | What's happening |
|---|---|
| Referral | The provider's office sends the order |
| Insurance Verification | Benefits and coverage confirmed |
| Documentation Request / Confirmation | Any additional paperwork requested from the provider, and confirmed when it arrives |
| Prior Authorization | Submitted to insurance where the plan requires it |
| Validation | Order details and documentation checked before release |
| Field Ops | Pushed to Field Ops; delivery scheduled and completed |

{{diagram:lifecycle}}

*The whole journey, both flows. Standard DME runs left to right along the top. A power mobility order runs through Sales, Power intake, then delivery.*

> **Note — Power Mobility works differently.** Power orders run **Sales → Power (PAK → Qualifications → PAR) → Field Ops-Power**. If you're handling a power mobility call, use [[§4-1]] rather than the sequence above.

### §0-8.1 Insurance verification teams

Insurance verification is handled by two teams, split by order type:

| Team | Verifies |
|---|---|
| **Eligibility MM & R** — Manual Mobility and Resupply | Manual mobility, general DME, respiratory and resupply orders |
| **Sales Eligibility** | Power mobility device orders — see [[§4-2]] |

Both teams **can** be contacted, though it's usually unnecessary. When a caller asks for detail during verification, the answer is normally that an update follows once verification completes.

| Team | Call queue | Email | Direct transfer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Eligibility MM & R** | Yes | `eligibility@universalmedsupply.com` | Yes |
| **Sales Eligibility** | None | `saleseligibility@universalmedsupply.com` | To the team's supervisor — `[ROLE: Insurance Eligibility — Sales]` |

> **Script** — "Your order is with our insurance verification team right now. They're confirming exactly what your plan covers, and as soon as that's done we'll reach out with an update or let you know if anything further is needed."

## §0-10 Anatomy of a transaction

The manual refers to these tabs constantly. This is where each thing lives.

{{diagram:transaction}}

> **Watch-out — three that are easy to confuse.** `Eligibility` tells you which **department** has a PMD order. `Pat. Resp.` tells you what the patient **owes**. Neither gives you the delivery date — that's `Ticket`.

> **Note — three things the manual refers to constantly are not in the left navigation.**
>
> | You want | It's behind |
> |---|---|
> | **Notes** | the **Messages** button, bottom right — it opens the Notes modal |
> | **Fax History** | a button inside the **Transaction** tab |
> | **Artifacts** — signed PRF, delivery photos | the **Patient Artifacts** and **Order Artifacts** buttons at the bottom |
>
> All three are referenced throughout the manual. See [[§0-11]], [[§0-2.2]] and [[§5-6]].


**Reading the Transactions page icons.** The Transactions page encodes most of what you need before you open anything. The five groups below show each icon and what it means.

> **Watch-out — the columns are read left to right, not as a single status.** A transaction has a
> **Trx Type**, a **Trx State**, an **Intake State** and a **Ticket State** at the same time, and
> each says something different. "Authorized with no truck symbol" is a validated order that hasn't
> been delivered — which is what [[§5-2]] means by an order being in the Field Ops grid.

## §0-11 Notes and email conventions

### §0-11.1 Notating a call

Notes open from the **Messages** button at the bottom right of the Transaction Workflow window.

Every call gets a note. A useful note answers three questions:

1. **Who called** — patient, provider's office, insurance representative, caregiver
2. **What they wanted**
3. **What you did or committed to**

Record reference numbers, fax numbers, appointment dates, and names of provider staff verbatim. These are the details someone else will need and cannot reconstruct.

The Notes tool's template has seven fields, in this order. Fill every one that applies:

| Field | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| **Callback Number** | The number to reach the caller on — confirm it, even if it's on the account |
| **Caller Name** | Who you spoke to, as they gave it |
| **Relationship** | The caller's relationship to the patient — self, spouse, daughter, the provider's office, an insurance representative |
| **Patient & TRX** | The patient's name and transaction number, or the TRX number alone |
| **Issue** | Why they called, in their words. Anything the template has no line for — a new address, a Medicare number, a reference number — goes here too |
| **Transferred To** | Who you transferred the call to, or leave it blank / N/A |
| **Resolution** | What you did or committed to, and what happens next |

### §0-11.2 Email subject format

One format for every internal email sent to a department inbox:

```
[Update type]: [Patient name] [TRX #]
```

| Update type | Example subject |
|---|---|
| Re-open Request | `Re-open Request: John Doe 123456` |
| Authorization Decision | `Authorization Decision: Jane Smith 789012` |
| Complaint | `Complaint: Robert Lee 345678` |
| OOP Purchase | `OOP Purchase: Maria Garcia 456789` |

The inbox tells the department who it's for; the update type tells them what it is before they open it.

> **Watch-out** — Include the TRX number every time. Without it the receiving team has to search by name, which is slow and error-prone when names are common.

### §0-11.3 What to include in the body

State what's needed and any deadline. If insurance gave you a decision or a request, include the reference number and the date it was received.

### §0-11.4 Fax numbers

| Fax | Number |
|---|---|
| **Main UMS fax** — the default for referrals and documents | **972-572-1112** |
| Sales department | 210-761-7887 — see [[§9-7.2]] |

## §0-12 Transfer, email, or notate

This is the most common judgment call in the role. Use this order.

{{diagram:routing}}

### §0-12.1 Notate only

The information needs recording but no one needs to act:

- Demographic and contact updates ([[§0-3]])
- Insurance details collected from a patient
- A caller confirming information we already have
- Any call where you fully answered the question

### §0-12.2 Transfer

The caller needs a specialist **now**, or immediate action would help:

- Complex billing questions, to Billing — `[ROLE: Billing Supervisor]`
- Compliance calls you can't resolve yourself — to the compliance specialists ([[§3-12]])
- An insurance representative **requesting** additional authorization information — to the relevant intake team's authorization members
- A provider's office with clinical questions you can't resolve — to the appropriate intake team: the specific sub-team or employee if you can identify them, otherwise the department queue
- Scheduling — to the Field Ops Q, or the Field Ops-Power Q for power mobility

Before transferring, notate what the caller wants so the receiving team isn't starting cold.

### §0-12.3 Email

Transfer isn't possible or is unnecessary:

- The specialist or department is unavailable
- The request needs action by another department, and isn't urgent or same-day time-sensitive
- A request about a closed order — email the department that last worked on or closed it ([[§0-2.2]])
- An out-of-pocket purchase you've completed — notify intake, eligibility and Field Operations ([[§0-6]])
- An insurance representative **giving** you an authorization decision — see below

> **Policy — taking an authorization decision.** When an insurance representative calls with a decision, transfer may not be necessary. Instead:
>
> 1. Note the **decision** — approved, denied, or other
> 2. Note the **authorization reference number**
> 3. Confirm the representative will also **fax or email the authorization response letter**
> 4. Post your notes on the transaction
> 5. Email the relevant intake team

> **Watch-out** — Transfers may be unnecessary if the receiving team will provide the same information that you did (unless the caller refused to accept your response and escalated). Orders needing re-opening, and questions during insurance verification, both fall into this category. Unnecessary transfers cost both teams and the caller time without added benefit.

### §0-12.4 Never

- Cold transfer — notate first, and tell the receiving team what the caller needs ([[§1-4.4]])
- Commit to a turnaround time you can't see in the system

**Generally avoid** giving a caller an individual employee's direct extension. Outbound callers often leave their extension on a voicemail, which is fine — but a patient who then asks for that person every time is working against how orders move. Each order passes through several stages and teams, so one person handling it from start to finish is not true to our process. Route the caller to whoever holds the order now.

## §0-13 General FAQ

Department-specific questions are in the FAQ section of each part.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| My primary denied it — can my secondary cover it? | Usually not the full cost — a secondary normally covers the remaining share on items the primary approves. **Texas Medicaid is the exception** for items Medicare never covers, such as shower chairs and incontinence supplies. See [[§0-7]]. |
| Can I just buy the equipment myself? | Yes for most items, at the out-of-pocket price in the Item Master. Oxygen concentrators, PAP devices and ventilators still need a prescription. Note that an out-of-pocket order **isn't eligible for a payment plan or the EAA**. See [[§0-6]]. |
| Why can't anyone tell me more while my insurance is being verified? | The verification team works the file directly and updates the order when complete. We update the patient as soon as that finishes — offer to answer any general questions in the meantime. See [[§0-8.1]]. |
| Do you take my insurance? | Most insurances are accepted, but it depends on the plan and the item. The reliable path is to have the referral sent for review. See [[§0-7]]. |
| Can I change an item on my order? | Usually yes, if the order is still in progress and hasn't been delivered. For a **power mobility device**, it depends on documentation from the provider and on the insurance's guidelines — see [[§4-1]]. After delivery, see [[§6-7]] |
| How long does this take? | It depends mostly on how quickly we get the **correct documents from the medical provider**. If everything arrives straight away, many orders are completed within a few days. If the provider takes weeks to send what's needed, the order can't move until they do. The same is true of power mobility, but the minimum timeframe is longer — see [[§4-1.2]] |


---

## §0-14 Outbound calls

Every call you place to a patient, caregiver or provider follows the same steps.

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| Open | Give your name and the company, say the call is **on a recorded line**, and say what you're calling about |
| No answer | Try again using **at least one other caller ID** from the 8x8 outbound list — at least **two attempts** in all |
| Voicemail | Leave the voicemail script below — **no patient details** |
| Note it | Note every attempt on the transaction: the time, the number you called, and the outcome |

> **Script — opening.** "Hello, this is (your name) with UniversalMed Supply on a recorded line, calling about…"

> **Script — voicemail.** "Hello, this is (your name) with UniversalMed Supply calling about your order. Please give me a callback at…"

> **Watch-out — no patient details on a voicemail.** Whoever plays the message back may not be the patient. Give your name, the company and a callback number — never the item, the diagnosis or a balance.

If the person you reach needs a Spanish speaker, see [[§1-8.2]].
